newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire's Kabila to send delegation to capital.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's Kabila to send delegation to capital.

text.p: Triumphant Laurent Kabila will send a delegation to the Zairean capital Kinshasa on Sunday to reassure the people about security and other concerns, a senior Alliance official said on Sunday.

The delegation was due to leave Lubumbashi within hours and would be headed by Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo Secretary-General Deogratius Bugera and included "information minister" Raphael Ghenda.
"When we take a town, we always send a team. They have to reassure the population and explain our message," said Mwawapanga Mwana Nanga, the rebel finance minister.
Asked when Kabila would go to the capital, he said: "In the next couple of days or a few days. It is at his discretion."

Kabila, 56, declared himself head of state in a statement he read at his headquarters in the southern mining city of Lubumbashi on Saturday as his forces moved into the capital Kinshasa virtually unopposed, to the cheers of residents.

The Organisation of African Unity (OAU) on Sunday acknowledged the civil war triumph of Kabila and his rebels and called for a broad-based transitional authority representing Zaireans of other political shades.
"Mr Kabila and the AFDL (rebel alliance) have won the civil war and the challenge before them now is to win and consolidate the peace," said OAU Secretary-General Salim Ahmed Salim.
"I hope that when Mr Kabila forms his government of transition, it will be a broad-based one, incorporating other elements of the Congo-Zaire society," Salim said in a statement.
